notes: Registered in docs/research/score-components-v1.md and bound by entry-signal-family-rules-v1.md. v2 resolves an ambiguity found before any relationship was computed: five components record both a raw `value` and a discretised 0-2 `points`, and this study reads `value`. The ingredient is the measurement; points is the composite's own discretisation and HYP-019 already found the composite ranks backwards. minimum_completed_trades counts EPISODES, one per pump event, not decision rows. The margins are read as ABSOLUTE spreads between the top and bottom quintile, because a component predicting the outcome downwards is as informative as one predicting it upwards. A candidate also requires monotonicity across all five quintiles. Sufficiency is checked before either verdict. v3 fixes a defect found after the v2 discovery read, in the measurement rather than in the rule: quintiles were formed by rank position, so a boundary could fall inside a tied value and split equal measurements by sort order. pump_age is recorded to a tenth of a minute and 368 of 821 discovery episodes read exactly 0.6, which put quintiles two and three wholly inside one value; oi_trend is worse, 606 of 821 sharing one value. Monotonicity across such a partition is produced by the sort and not by the component, so a candidate now also requires that every adjacent pair of quintiles differ in the component. The change is strictly stricter: it can withdraw a candidate and can never create one, which is why it is applied to an already-read window rather than deferred.
